_doc: Single source of truth for the village look. Every leaf is {v, why}. Read by scripts/look.gd; documented in docs/art-pipeline.md. Change values here, never in scene code.

far_fov.why: vertical degrees; near-orthographic like a pre-rendered iso game

near_fov.why: mid view becomes a natural perspective around the character

far_width.why: metres of ground across the screen; closer than 22 m so building and material detail reads

near_width.why: mid view frames the character plus their surroundings

far_pitch.why: steep ARPG look-down; walls still visible

near_pitch.why: flatter at mid range so faces of buildings fill more of the frame

tonemap_exposure.why: AgX exposure; lit ground lands near the 0.45 target

tonemap_white.why: AgX white point; keeps sunlit plaster from clipping

adjustment_contrast.why: neutral: extra contrast crushed shadows to black (art review 2)

ambient_sky_contribution.why: mostly neutral grey fill: the blue HDRI sky cast blue shadows (b/r 1.1-1.3, review 3)

ambient_energy_day.why: only used where SDFGI does not reach; with SDFGI on, Godot ignores ambient energy/colour for GI-covered surfaces (measured: no effect)

sdfgi_energy.why: THE fill knob with SDFGI on (sky + bounce): shadow floor 0.20-0.26 at far and mid (art check)

ssao_radius.why: metres; tight contact occlusion at bases, crevices come from baked AO

ssao_intensity.why: contact darkening; 3.5 stacked with the skirt into black halos (review 3)

ssao_power.why: sharpens the falloff so it reads as contact, not haze

ssil_radius.why: metres of screen-space bounce (walls onto ground)

ssil_intensity.why: screen-space bounce; was 0.25 against magenta bounce off the old plank barn (now daub); shadow_green guards it

sky_saturation.why: HDRI sky partly desaturated: under SDFGI the sky IS the shadow fill; full blue gave shadows a blue cast (art check shadow_tint 1.25)

sky_energy.why: sky brightness = shadow fill under SDFGI; tuned so shadowed ground sits at 0.20-0.26 (art check)

night_sky_energy.why: sky (= GI fill) at night: readable moonlit night, not black (user default 2026-10-16)

sky_energy_low.why: sky fill (x day) when the sun is low (same ramp as the sun colour): the real sky dims with the sun; at full fill the 17 deg dusk sun barely showed (key:fill 1.4, 2026-10-16). Swept 2026-10-16: 0.45 -> dusk key:fill 2.0, 0.25 -> 3.8

exposure_low.why: exposure (x tonemap_exposure) as the sun nears the horizon, daylight only: the camera exposes up for golden hour instead of the frame going dark. 4.0 keeps the dusk frame at 0.24 with the dimmer sky (swept 2.5-4.0)

sky_saturation_low.why: sky saturation as the sun nears the horizon (same ramp as the sun colour): the blue sky keeps golden-hour shade neutral-cool instead of orange bounce (Fable round 6: dusk read as an orange filter)

energy_day.why: key light; ~4:1 against the fill. 3.2 -> 3.3 (round 7): denser square content put far.lit_mean at 0.397

angular_distance.why: degrees; soft penumbra like the pre-rendered references (0.5 read as hard real-time shadows)

peak_elevation.why: noon elevation; long enough shadows to model form

yaw_at_noon.why: degrees; upper-left key light; at 75 the barn's camera-facing wall was edge-on to the sun (review 3). 50 -> 55 with 15 deg/h keeps the 11:00 shots' sun exactly where it was (40 deg)

yaw_per_hour.why: sun moves across the sky during the day. 10 -> 15 deg/h (round 11, the real sun's mean rate): 9:00 looked like noon (Fable r11)

shadow_normal_bias.why: no acne on gently curved thatch

shadow_margin.why: metres added to the fitted shadow range beyond the farthest visible ground

moon_energy.why: moonlight key at night; torches stay the brightest light

energy_low.why: sun energy floor (x day energy) while low above the horizon: golden hour, not dusk-dark (review 5)

warm_below_elevation.why: degrees; sun colour follows a smoothstep from color_low (horizon) to color_day at this elevation: flat near noon, fast near the horizon. Linear over 20 left the 17 deg dusk barely warm (key warmth 1.05, 2026-10-16); 45 + smoothstep: dusk 1.63, 9:00 1.09 (neutral, checks.morning)

triplanar_tiles.why: tiles per metre for world-triplanar placeholder geometry

triplanar_tint.why: leafy_grass reads as dry dirt from above; push it to green

weathered._why: per material slot of scripted assets (tools/blender), parameters of shaders/weathered.gdshader. roughness_min/specular: the scanned roughness maps are glossy; at 0.5 specular the thatch's brightness was mostly sky reflection, flattening every albedo change (review 4 roof structure)

stone.why: moss on stone footings and chimneys

plaster.why: pale lime daub on the white flaking scan; dark timber frame must read against it (round 6: grey_plaster_03 x warm tint made a tan slab, frame lost). Splash dirt up to ~1 m

timber.why: the Poly Haven planks are very dark; lifted so lit planks reach ~0.18+

thatch.why: straw-yellow aged thatch; detile hides the tile period; eave_age darkens and moss-greens the lower courses (review 4: roof was one flat plane). Courses (coordinator default 2026-10-16): subtle horizontal bands every 0.2 m of height (~0.28 m along a 45 deg slope, matching roofs.py), dark under each butt edge, +-12% tone per course. Round 7: pale desaturated straw [0.85,0.75,0.5] (was orange-brown 0.8/0.62/0.36) and course_shadow 0.6 (0.3 barely visible); A/B ab/thatch_straw: roof_macro 0.057 -> 0.065. Round 8: tint 1.45/1.26/0.84 (> 1 lifts the dark scan): lit thatch 0.29 -> ~0.5, level with lit grass like The Guild (checks.far.thatch_vs_grass); A/B ab/thatch_bright*. Round 9: bundles 0.3 m wide along each course with own tone (bundle_var 0.2), dark gaps (0.5) and jagged butt ends (ragged 0.4): reads as laid straw, not fur. Stronger (0.35/0.8/0.6) read as shingles; the remaining bundle-scale gap to The Guild (checks.far.thatch_bundles) needs geometric depth. Tint 1.52/1.32/0.88 keeps thatch level with grass. bundle_relief 0.6 (round 9): shader normals round each bundle and step each course, so the sun lights one flank (A/B ab/relief*: thatch_bundles 0.037 -> 0.054); real geometry would cost ~30k tris per roof (longhouse at 95k of 100k). Tint 1.57/1.37/0.91 keeps it level with grass. Round 10: no hard bundle cells (Fable r9: read as shingles): bundle tone, gaps and the butt-end line vary smoothly along the course; relief keeps the stepped courses, only a slight along-course wobble. A/B ab/straw

cloth.why: undyed coarse burlap (hessian_230); no edge wear (it lightened folds into rusty metal, review 3). Round 8: own texture instead of the plaster scan, which made the stall canvas the brightest, plaster-like surface

weathered_common.why: shared by every slot; splash/grime lowered in art review 2 (they crushed timber to 0.09). ao_strength 1.0 -> 0.7 (Fable round 6 A/B): contacts stacked vertex AO + skirt + SSAO

leaves.why: summer oak (~10% reflectance); per-plant variation. interior_value 0.35 -> 0.55 (round 8): crowns read as rounded green masses, not black holes

water.why: dark green river; rough, low-specular surface (review 5: glints read as white noise); shallower depth scale so the bed shows. Round 10: ripple normal strength 0.35, roughness 0.25, darker shallows: the full-strength ripples caught the sky as white dashes (Fable r5-r10); The Guild's river is dark with fine ripples. A/B ab/water_calm

ground.why: darkens bright scans so lit ground sits near 0.45; grass and soil tints carry the scene's chroma (grade stays neutral). grass_tint -8% (round 8): lit grass 0.50 -> ~0.46, inside The Guild lawn 0.45-0.60, lets thatch read level with it. Round 11: grass->dirt edge wider (edge_width 0.2) and broken into ~10 cm clumps (edge_clumps 0.4, edge_break 0.75): Fable r10 'hard mask with a gravel rim'. A/B ab/grass_edge

flat.why: untextured slots and placeholders (player capsule, torch post, window voids)

waterline_wander.why: metres of noise on the bank shelf so the waterline is never a ruler line (review 3)

skirt.why: dirt skirt decal under every placed building/prop (rule, automatic); mid-brown at 60% so contact reads as soil, not a black halo (review 3)

grass_points.why: candidate tuft positions; noise clustering keeps about half

grass_keep.why: base keep probability before noise clustering

grass_tuft.why: few short blades, tip close to root colour: tufts read as texture, never as countable dark starbursts (review 3)

debris_points.why: about one small detail per square metre near paths and houses

tree_clearance.why: metres; crowns never hang over the river, houses or paths

keep_off_paths.why: props that must never block a path or yard; dropped if placed on trampled ground (mask > 0.3)

grass_tuft_shadows.why: tuft shadows made dark stars at the far view (review 3)

debris_colors.why: albedo before the ground_value darkening shared with the ground, so debris sits in the ground's value range (review 4: chips were bright orange flecks)

torch.why: torches lit around sunset (day factor follows elevation -2..+4 deg) and the brightest light at night; unlit by day

garden.why: kitchen garden rows behind every house: fills back yards like The Guild (density check far.empty_share)

yard_tree.why: one smaller oak behind/beside every house, away from the square: trees among the buildings without the crowns covering the view (review 5; at 52° down a full-size crown hid a quarter of the frame)

debris_min_dirt.why: no debris on untrampled grass except along walls

bush_crown_overlap.why: a bush is dropped if its crown radius x this plus a prop's footprint radius exceeds their distance (both from mesh bounds): the flat 1.1 m clearance missed bush_2 at scale 1.3 (1.7 m crown, rounds 7-8). < 1: outer leaves may brush a prop

checks._why: tools/art_check.py on the captured far/mid shots. Each is rendered three times: full, sun off (_fill: classifies lit vs shadow pixels so checks follow the sun) and lighting-only (_light: white albedo, measures the colour of the light itself).

lit_mean.why: mean value of sunlit pixels (sun adds >5x the sun-off frame)

shadow_tint.why: blue/red of the light in shadow (lighting-only pass): skylit shade slightly cool is natural; review 3's fault was a strong blue cast

contact_floor.why: 1st percentile of the frame blurred 8 px: contacts dark but never black halos (reference measures 0.05-0.07)

shadow_green.why: g/avg(r,b) of the light in shadow (lighting-only pass): no magenta bounce off red walls (review 4)

grass_speckle.why: share of open-grass pixels brighter than median+0.15: tufts/debris must not read as sprinkles (region left of the stall)

saturation.why: mean HSL saturation of sunlit pixels (AgX correctly desaturates shade, review 5); colour from materials, grade neutral

empty_share.why: share of ~1.3 m blocks with almost no detail: The Guild never shows an empty patch (2026-10-16: 0.26)

key_fill.why: light on sunlit vs shadowed surfaces (lighting-only pass, linear): ~4:1 key:fill. Replaces shadow_mean, which mixed albedo in: mid shadow pixels are dark soil (0.5x lit albedo), far ones 1.9x, so no single fill could satisfy both (2026-10-16 sweep)

thatch_vs_grass.why: lit thatch at or above lit grass in value (sRGB, ID pass). Measured on docs/reference/the-guild/guild3_3.jpg: lit thatch 0.57, lit lawn 0.45-0.60 -> ~1.0-1.25 (Fable round 7 estimated 2.7; the reference measurement overrides it). Round 7: 0.59

thatch_saturation.why: lit thatch straw saturation within the reference range: measured guild3_3 0.40, guild3_1 0.60 (Fable round 7 estimated 0.29; reference measurement overrides it)

leaves_value.why: lit foliage reads as green masses, not near-black holes: >= 60/255 (Fable round 7, bushes measured ~39/255). Set before tuning

cloth_value.why: lit stall canvas / sacks no brighter than 130/255: the canvas was the brightest surface and pulled the eye off the well (Fable round 7). Set before tuning

thatch_bundles.why: bundle-scale detail on lit thatch: sd of (blur 3 px - blur 12 px). The Guild measures 0.092 (guild3_3 250x100+300+110) and 0.093 (guild3_1 400x200+700+120) at the same course spacing as our far view (~33 px); round 8: 0.036 (smooth fur). Set before tuning

roof_macro.why: 16 px-blurred std dev over lit thatch (ID pass; was a fixed rect on the barn roof, which the yard oak's shadow now covers, Fable r7). Target unchanged (review 5: lowering it to 0.05 was fitting the check)

foliage_clusters.why: crowns read as lit clusters with shadowed gaps, not uniform confetti: 8 px-blurred sd over all leaf pixels. The Guild trees 0.095 (guild3_3 400x300+1500+0) and 0.112 (250x150+1000+0); round 10: 0.071. Set before tuning

lit_mean.why: mean value of sunlit pixels (sun adds >5x the sun-off frame)

shadow_tint.why: blue/red of the light in shadow (lighting-only pass): skylit shade slightly cool is natural; review 3's fault was a strong blue cast

contact_floor.why: 1st percentile of the frame blurred 8 px: contacts dark but never black halos (reference measures 0.05-0.07)

shadow_green.why: g/avg(r,b) of the light in shadow (lighting-only pass): no magenta bounce off red walls (review 4)

saturation.why: mean HSL saturation of sunlit pixels (AgX correctly desaturates shade, review 5); colour from materials, grade neutral

key_fill.why: light on sunlit vs shadowed surfaces (lighting-only pass, linear): ~4:1 key:fill. Replaces shadow_mean, which mixed albedo in: mid shadow pixels are dark soil (0.5x lit albedo), far ones 1.9x, so no single fill could satisfy both (2026-10-16 sweep)

budgets.why: max triangles per GLB on an M2 Pro

mean.why: night readable like Baldur's Gate 2 (~0.15), not black (user default)

torch_brightest.why: mean of the torch's light pool / frame mean: the torch is clearly the brightest area at night

dusk._why: godot_far_dusk at 16:48 (sun ~16° high): golden hour. 17:36 had the sun at 6°, i.e. sunset, not golden hour

lit_mean.why: whole frame at golden hour stays a daylight frame (review 5). 0.30 -> 0.22, user decision 2026-10-16: a 16-17 deg sun lights flat ground at ~0.29 of noon, so golden hour is judged by warmth and contrast, not brightness (docs/art-check-conflicts.md)

key_warmth.why: red/blue of the light on sunlit surfaces (lighting-only pass): noon sun [1,0.96,0.9] gives ~1.1; golden hour clearly warm (>= 1.5) but not sunset orange (<= 2.5). Set before measuring. user decision 2026-10-16 (“改看暖色”): golden hour is judged by warmth and contrast, not brightness (docs/art-check-conflicts.md)

key_fill.why: a low sun still models form: key:fill at least the daytime 3, up to 6 (long, deeper shadows). Set before measuring. user decision 2026-10-16 (“改看暖色”): golden hour is judged by warmth and contrast, not brightness (docs/art-check-conflicts.md)

shadow_tint.why: blue/red of the light in shadow (lighting-only pass): at golden hour only the key is warm, the shade stays neutral or cool (Fable round 6: R/B <= 1.15)

saturation.why: whole-frame HSL saturation: golden hour, not an orange filter (round 6 measured 0.48 vs 0.33 at noon)

light_pass_exposure.why: exposure of the lighting-only measurement pass, rendered with the linear tonemapper so the brightest sunlit light stays below 1.0 (no clipping) and keeps its colour

morning._why: godot_far_morning at 9:00 (sun ~39 deg): daylight must stay neutral (user: neutral grade); the golden-hour colour ramp must not tint it

key_warmth.why: red/blue of the key light on lit pixels: noon measures 1.05; a visibly orange morning would read > 1.15

id_colors.why: material classes in the ID pass (_id.png): per-surface checks measure one material, not a frame mix of albedos (round 6-7 lesson). Slots not listed emit black = unclassified; colours far apart after normalising by the max channel
